target_frame.title: Intermittent cold-room delivery gaps
target_frame.problem: A regional food distributor finds that some refrigerated deliveries arrive above its internal receiving temperature range, although the loading records show acceptable temperatures. The operations manager must decide what to investigate next and which temporary handling changes are justified before the next fortnight of deliveries.
known_context: There are three loading bays, two contracted carriers and routes lasting between forty minutes and four hours.
Drivers record departure and arrival times; receiving staff take a single temperature reading from one package per delivery.
Loading-bay logs record room temperature every fifteen minutes, but packages are not individually tracked between staging and loading.
The recent exceptions occur on both short and long routes. Receiving methods differ between customer sites.
A small pool of reusable temperature loggers is available, but the team cannot instrument every package or cancel routine deliveries.
target_frame.uncertainty: The manager does not know whether the exceptions mainly arise before loading, in transit, during receiving, or from differences in measurement. Multiple contributors may be present.
target_frame.decision_need: Identify a feasible investigation and defensible interim action without claiming that the existing endpoint records locate the cause.
constraints: Normal food-handling requirements remain in force.
Staff can add limited observations for two weeks; there is no budget for fleet replacement.

current_position.statement: The cause remains unresolved; staging/loading, transit, receiving and measurement differences may contribute together.
current_position.rationale: Acceptable loading-room temperatures and one receiving package reading do not locate when package temperatures changed. Exceptions on short and long routes do not isolate transit duration.

top_uncertainties.uncertainty: Where and when affected packages become elevated.
top_uncertainties.why_it_matters: The appropriate handling change depends on the stage involved.

top_uncertainties.uncertainty: Whether receiving readings are reliable and comparable across sites.
top_uncertainties.why_it_matters: Different methods may create or obscure apparent exceptions.

next_inquiries.inquiry: Establish whether limited package-linked monitoring is interpretable.
next_inquiries.operation_or_observation: Before deployment, define and verify logger-to-package identification, sensor placement, clock alignment and handoff recording. Establish what each sensor measures and whether its response can distinguish relevant stages.
next_inquiries.decision_relevance: Unverified linkage or inadequate timing prevents reliable package or stage attribution.

next_inquiries.inquiry: Observe selected deliveries across relevant operating conditions.
next_inquiries.operation_or_observation: Propose a feasible two-week logger rotation covering both carriers, all three bays, short and long routes, and differing receiving practices as capacity permits. Track selected packages through staging, loading, arrival and receipt measurement; record handoff times and delays.
next_inquiries.decision_relevance: This can reveal stage-specific patterns in monitored cases; incomplete coverage limits wider conclusions.

next_inquiries.inquiry: Compare usual and standardized receiving measurements where feasible.
next_inquiries.operation_or_observation: On a verified tracked package, pair usual and standardized readings without compromising handling. Document method, location and delay; first establish reference reliability, timing/location tolerances and possible shared errors.
next_inquiries.decision_relevance: Interpretable disagreement supports investigating measurement differences; reliable agreement on elevation weakens those differences as the sole explanation.

priorities.item: Secure interpretable observations before expanding monitoring.
priorities.rationale: More readings will not resolve the cause if package identity, measurement meaning or timing is uncertain.

priorities.item: Compare competing explanations, then target remaining ambiguities.
priorities.rationale: Reliable contradictions and observations distinguishing surviving alternatives matter more than counts of supporting readings.

immediate_actions.action: Before reviewing new results, write expected observations for each stage and measurement explanation, including combinations.
immediate_actions.rationale: Explicit predictions make subsequent comparisons assessable.

immediate_actions.action: During the fortnight, minimize avoidable staging and receiving delays within existing food-handling requirements; record any changes.
immediate_actions.rationale: This is a limited precaution against possible exposure, not evidence that delays caused the exceptions.

immediate_actions.action: Use a common approved receiving method where it can provide reliable, comparable readings within staff capacity.
immediate_actions.rationale: Standardization can improve interpretation, but approval or uniformity alone does not establish reliability.

decision_rules.condition: Reliable package-linked observations distinguish temperatures before and after a stage.
decision_rules.consequence: Elevation already present before loading supports investigating staging/loading; a subsequent rise supports investigating the stage containing that rise.
decision_rules.rationale: These patterns inform monitored cases and may support multiple contributors; they do not establish a unique cause.

decision_rules.consequence: Compare each explanation against them as consistent, inconsistent or indeterminate, recording reasons and confidence. Weight reliable contradictions by importance and treat repeated records within a delivery as dependent.
decision_rules.rationale: Supporting counts can exaggerate evidence and conceal consequential contradictions.

decision_rules.condition: Readings or stage boundaries are uncertain.
decision_rules.consequence: Repeat comparisons excluding unreliable readings and varying plausible handoff times and sensor-response assumptions. Mark affected comparisons indeterminate when resolution, placement or comparability is inadequate.
decision_rules.rationale: Lag, clock/device errors, package variation and measurement locations can create apparent contradictions.

important_distinctions.distinction: Surrounding-air temperature and package temperature are different measurements.
important_distinctions.consequence: Use air records as contextual evidence without treating them as direct package-temperature readings.

important_distinctions.distinction: Evidence against an explanation in monitored cases differs from excluding it across operations.
important_distinctions.consequence: Restrict any elimination to the conditions actually tested and supported by reliable evidence.

constraints.constraint: Food-handling requirements remain in force and routine deliveries must continue.
constraints.implication: Monitoring and paired measurements must fit safe handling without delaying deliveries unnecessarily.

constraints.constraint: Logger availability and added staff observations are limited to a two-week effort; fleet replacement is unfunded.
constraints.implication: Use selective monitoring and feasible handling changes, and explicitly report coverage gaps.

do_not_conclude.statement: Missing or failed traces show that a stage was satisfactory.
do_not_conclude.reason: Absent evidence is inconclusive; retain only interpretable portions of affected records.

do_not_conclude.statement: The fortnight necessarily ends with a causal diagnosis.
do_not_conclude.reason: Unstable rankings or inadequate coverage block a causal declaration. Sensitivity to omitted mechanisms, subjective judgments or shared assumptions requires an explicitly uncertain conclusion.

current_position.statement: The reported receiving exceptions warrant investigation, but existing records do not locate their cause. Multiple contributors remain plausible.
current_position.rationale: Loading logs measure room temperature, packages are untracked between staging and loading, and receiving uses one package reading with methods that vary by site. Exceptions occur on both short and long routes.

top_uncertainties.uncertainty: Where and when temperature changes occur.
top_uncertainties.why_it_matters: Staging, loading, transit and receiving require different corrective actions.

top_uncertainties.uncertainty: How much receiving methods contribute to the reported exceptions.
top_uncertainties.why_it_matters: Different methods and single-package sampling limit comparability and delivery-wide conclusions.

top_uncertainties.uncertainty: Whether exceptions share one cause or reflect several contributors.
top_uncertainties.why_it_matters: A single change may leave other sources of temperature deviation unresolved.

next_inquiries.inquiry: Follow selected packages across the delivery process.
next_inquiries.operation_or_observation: For two weeks, rotate available loggers through identified sample packages from staging through receiving. Record logger placement and staging, loading, departure, arrival and receiving-reading times.
next_inquiries.decision_relevance: Relates temperature changes to handling intervals instead of inferring cause from endpoints.

next_inquiries.operation_or_observation: Document site methods, package selection and delay before measurement. On sampled deliveries, add a common measurement procedure and, where feasible, readings from additional packages.
next_inquiries.decision_relevance: Tests whether method differences or package variation help explain reported exceptions.

next_inquiries.operation_or_observation: Distribute the limited samples across all three bays, both carriers, short and long routes, and differing receiving sites. Link each sample to its bay, carrier, route and receiving method; repeat informative comparisons where feasible.
next_inquiries.decision_relevance: Identifies patterns worth targeting while reducing reliance on isolated events.

priorities.item: Make sampled temperature readings comparable and link them to packages and handling times.
priorities.rationale: These gaps currently prevent reliable interpretation.

priorities.item: Obtain temperature histories spanning staging through receiving.
priorities.rationale: Locating the interval of change is more actionable than collecting additional unlinked endpoint readings.

priorities.item: Use emerging evidence to focus repeat observations.
priorities.rationale: Logger capacity and staff time are limited.

immediate_actions.action: Reinforce required cold handling and reduce avoidable staging, loading and receiving delays.
immediate_actions.rationale: This is a defensible temporary precaution while the responsible interval remains unknown.

immediate_actions.action: Assign logger rotation, sample identification and a short shared observation record before the next deliveries.
immediate_actions.rationale: The two-week investigation needs consistent execution with limited equipment.

immediate_actions.action: Apply existing food-handling requirements to out-of-range deliveries while documenting the measurement and handling circumstances.
immediate_actions.rationale: The investigation does not suspend normal handling requirements.

decision_rules.condition: Repeated, comparable observations locate temperature increases within a particular handling interval.
decision_rules.consequence: Target corrective action and further monitoring at that interval.
decision_rules.rationale: Time-linked evidence supports a more specific intervention.

decision_rules.condition: Reported exceptions vary with measurement procedure or measurement delay.
decision_rules.consequence: Standardize the relevant receiving practice and reassess exceptions while continuing temperature tracing.
decision_rules.rationale: Measurement effects may explain part of the pattern without excluding handling problems.

decision_rules.condition: The two-week sample remains mixed or inconclusive.
decision_rules.consequence: Retain proportionate precautions and focus further sampling on unresolved intervals or conditions.
decision_rules.rationale: Limited coverage cannot establish a single cause or demonstrate that the problem has disappeared.

important_distinctions.distinction: Loading-room temperature differs from the temperature history of an individual package.
important_distinctions.consequence: Acceptable bay logs do not establish acceptable package conditions throughout staging and loading.

important_distinctions.distinction: One package reading differs from a delivery-wide assessment.
important_distinctions.consequence: Avoid treating a single reading as representative of every package.

constraints.constraint: Routine deliveries must continue, logger coverage is limited, and additional observations are feasible for two weeks.
constraints.implication: Use rotating samples and brief records rather than universal instrumentation.

constraints.constraint: Normal food-handling requirements remain in force, and fleet replacement has no budget.
constraints.implication: Keep interim changes within required handling practices and available operating resources.

do_not_conclude.statement: Acceptable loading logs prove the carrier caused the receiving exceptions.
do_not_conclude.reason: Pre-loading package conditions and receiving effects remain unresolved.

do_not_conclude.statement: Route duration alone explains the problem.
do_not_conclude.reason: Exceptions occur on both short and long routes; duration may still contribute alongside other factors.
